Consult Summary:
- 53-year-old man with one week of a non-painful, slightly warm swelling over the tip of the left elbow; clinician assesses likely bursitis and arranges NSAID therapy and blood tests with planned follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Noted swelling of left elbow for about one week, first noticed in the shower.
  - Describes it as a weird/visible swelling at the tip of the elbow.
  - Not painful at rest; slightly warm; feels like fluid inside the swelling.
  - Able to move the elbow normally; no known preceding trauma.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Onset approximately one week prior to the consult.
  - Patient reports it "feels a bit better now" at the end of the visit.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - No specific exacerbating or relieving factors mentioned.
- Associated symptoms / systems review:
  - Mild local discomfort when pressing adjacent to the swelling; tip itself largely not painful.
  - No systemic symptoms documented (fever, chills, malaise not mentioned).
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No history of prior similar episodes.
  - No known spreading redness, severe pain, or features suggestive of acute septic arthritis at presentation.

Past Medical History:
- Osteoarthritis — diagnosed by a GP a few years ago.
- No other chronic medical conditions reported.
- Allergies:
  - Peanut allergy (food).
  - No known drug allergies reported.

Medications:
- Regular medications: None reported.
- Acute/initiated during consult:
  - Ibuprofen 400 mg, twice daily after food (dose and frequency documented by clinician).
- Allergies: peanut (food).

Social History:
- Occupation/lifestyle:
  - Desk-based job (not physically demanding).
  - Regular exercise: runs 2–3 times per week; describes himself as generally fit and well.
- Tobacco / alcohol / recreational drugs:
  - Use not documented in the transcript.

Family History:
- No known family history of rheumatologic diseases reported; patient uncertain about family history.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Examination findings:
  - Left elbow: visible swelling at the tip/olecranon region.
  - Area slightly warmer compared with adjacent skin.
  - Mild discomfort when pressing adjacent to the swelling; tip of the elbow tolerates pressure.
  - Skin over tip noted as a bit dry.
  - Range of motion: patient able to move elbow normally.
- No other examination findings documented.

Investigations:
- Planned investigations (forms to be sent to the patient):
  - Blood tests: inflammatory markers, infection markers, rheumatologic antibody screen, and tests to screen for gout.
  - No laboratory results available at time of consult.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Left elbow swelling — probable bursitis (clinician impression)
  - Assessment:
    - Clinical appearance consistent with bursitis (inflammation of a fluid sac around the joint).
    - Septic arthritis considered unlikely at this presentation.
  - Plan:
    - Start ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food; stop if significant heartburn or intolerance.
    - Send blood test forms to patient for inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, and gout testing.
    - Expected turnaround for results: approximately 5–6 days after blood draw (forms may delay timing).
    - Arrange follow-up after blood tests; follow-up may be face-to-face, phone, or video per patient preference.
    - Advise patient to seek urgent review (phone/video or in-person) if elbow becomes very red, very painful, or the redness spreads — these would be emergency features requiring immediate assessment.
- Issue 2: Osteoarthritis (past medical history)
  - Assessment:
    - Documented history of osteoarthritis diagnosed by GP several years ago.
  - Plan:
    - No change to chronic disease management documented in this consult.
- General plan items:
  - Forms for blood tests to be mailed to the patient with instructions where to attend for phlebotomy.
  - Follow-up to review clinical status and blood test results; patient to contact clinic after blood tests or sooner if worsening.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (temperature, blood pressure, heart rate, respiratory rate) not recorded.
  - No imaging or aspiration performed; no synovial fluid analysis documented.
  - Exact blood test panel and specific laboratory test names not itemized beyond categories discussed.
  - Medication allergy reconciliation and confirmation of over-the-counter medication use beyond stated ibuprofen not documented.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - None identified.
- Transcript quality:
  - Conversation clear and audible; clinician and patient statements adequately documented.
